topic: A person discovers their child has the same teacher they had
text: The news of Eliza sharing a teacher with me, back from those days, leaves my mouth dry as the soil in high summer. I recall old Brother Augustine’s stern face, the way he watched over every misstep, and the lash of his tongue that still seems to sting. It’s a weight on my chest, thinking of my girl facing the same. I pray to Saint Isidore at night, and work the fields harder, hoping the sun will burn away the worries, but the thoughts of Eliza in that classroom shadow my days. I have to trust in the Harvest, and that the seeds we plant now, no matter how small or scared, will grow strong.
